report.summary: Unhandled SyntaxError in literal/structure layers crashes measure on invalid mutation; type layer silently swallows SyntaxError, hiding detection. Specificity arm is incomplete. Non-atomic JSON write risks corruption.

risks.finding: Unhandled SyntaxError in _literal_keys, _structure_keys, etc. causes measure() to crash when a mutation yields invalid Python, halting the entire run() and losing results for all mutations.
risks.trigger: Mutation that produces syntactically invalid code (e.g., deleting a colon).

risks.finding: _type_edge_keys catches SyntaxError and returns an empty set, silently reporting no delta for the type layer even though parsing failed, potentially missing a detection.
risks.trigger: Mutation making the file unparseable (SyntaxError) while the type layer is active.

risks.finding: The specificity arm (measure_commit, commit_shas) is truncated and non-functional, contradicting the module's documentation that it will compare real commits.
risks.trigger: Calling measure_commit raises NameError or AttributeError due to incomplete code.

risks.finding: Main writes JSON directly without atomic rename; on Windows, if the process is killed mid-write, the output file may be corrupted.

todos: Wrap ast.parse calls in literal and structure layers with try/except SyntaxError; on failure, skip the layer and set a skipped_reason or mark mutation as unapplied
In _type_edge_keys, log or propagate parse errors instead of silently returning empty set
Either complete or remove the specificity arm to match the docstring
Use atomic write (temp file + rename) for graph_delta.json output

handoff.suggestion: Add SyntaxError handling in _literal_keys and _structure_keys, similar to _ast_refs, to fail gracefully and record the error. In _type_edge_keys, do not silently return empty set on SyntaxError; either re-raise or mark the layer as failed in the result.
